title: Ghezelbash 2020: trunk EMG (%MVC) vs forward flexion holding 14 kg at four load heights, symmetric (19 subjects)
condition: static forward flexion with 14 kg hand load at upright, mid-femur, knee and mid-tibia heights, symmetric (A = 0 deg)

quantity.name: normalised EMG
quantity.definition: surface EMG RMS (30-450 Hz band-pass, 50 ms window) averaged over the static hold, normalised to the maximal RMS over six MVE directions in the semi-seated triaxial dynamometer (Ghezelbash 2018); left and right averaged (mean of the two sides; SD = mean of the two side SDs); mean +/- SD of 19 subjects

source.authors: Ghezelbash F, Shirazi-Adl A, El-Ouaaid Z, Plamondon A, Arjmand N
source.sample: 19 healthy adults (9 F, 10 M), same cohort as Ghezelbash 2018 and 2024; file in donwload/ is misnamed 'Mitutoyo Digital Caliper - Certificate of Calibration Control # DDE14R52L.PDF' (IRSST accepted manuscript)

protocol.summary: Standing, knees straight; 14 kg held statically in both hands at four load heights (umbilicus = upright, mid-femur, knee, mid-tibia), symmetric (A = 0 deg), load at a fixed horizontal distance 0.2xBH from the feet; each task once. Trunk flexion F = angle of the T11 axis from upright (Supplementary Material 2, Eq. S2-4). flexion_deg = trunk flexion measured with 10 kg at the same heights (Ghezelbash 2024 Fig 3c: 18.3/50.5/68.1/92.1 deg); flexion with 14 kg is not reported.
how_to_simulate: Scale to the mean subject (169.3 cm, 66.9 kg) or each sex
Static trunk flexion at data[].flexion_deg (or flex the trunk until the hands reach data[].load_height), knees straight, no asymmetry
14 kg (137 N) in both hands, horizontal distance 0.2xBH from the feet
Output: activation under each electrode (left/right mean), normalised to the model's maximal activity over six maximal exertions

subject_model.source: Ghezelbash 2020 J Biomech 102:109550 Methods lines 46-48; weighted means of the two sexes

protocol.notes: Derived view of the symmetric (A = 0) bars of Figs 5-6 already stored per side in the msk_emg_posture.ghezelbash2020.* tests (same digitisation, left and right averaged here), so the 14 kg data can be plotted against trunk flexion next to the 10 kg data (msk_flexion_relaxation.ghezelbash2024.emg_vs_flexion_10kg, same subjects). The flexion angle of each load height is taken from the 10 kg trials (Ghezelbash 2024 Fig 3c); the heavier load may change the angle by a few degrees, so simulate by load height if possible. 'Upright' = umbilicus-level hold (inference from Methods vs caption wording). Averaging the two side SDs slightly overestimates the SD of the bilateral mean. Model bars in Figs 5-6 are NOT data. Do not pool with the msk_emg_posture.ghezelbash2020.* tests (same data).

extraction.from: Fig 5 (MF L4, IC T11/L3, LG T11) and Fig 6 (RA, EO, IO), A = 0 deg groups (IRSST manuscript p.26-27), via the per-side values in msk_emg_posture.ghezelbash2020.*; flexion angles from Ghezelbash 2024 bioRxiv Fig 3c
extraction.uncertainty: mean +/-1 %MVC, SD +/-1.5 %MVC (300 dpi bar charts, per side); flexion angle +/-0.5 deg (400 dpi) plus unknown change from 10 to 14 kg
extraction.check_notes: Bilateral means computed from the checked per-side tests.
